sources.population_2024: OCHA HPC 2024 projection, HDX cod-ps-cod (summed from health zones)
sources.qualitative_fields: compiled from public literature; see Excel Sources sheet

meta.caveat: Last national census: 1984. All population figures are projections.

provinces.name: Kinshasa
provinces.economy_specialties: Administration, services, commerce, light industry, river port of Kinshasa
provinces.particularities: Capital and city-province; largest French-speaking city in the world; faces Brazzaville across the Congo River (closest capital pair in the world)
provinces.education: Université de Kinshasa (UNIKIN), UPN, UPC and dozens of institutions; highest literacy in the country

provinces.name: Kongo-Central
provinces.natural_resources: Offshore/onshore oil (Muanda), hydropower (Inga I & II, planned Grand Inga), bauxite, limestone
provinces.economy_specialties: Ports of Matadi and Boma (country's main import corridor), cement, oil production
provinces.particularities: Only province with an Atlantic coastline (~37 km); Inga dams on the Congo River have the world's largest hydropower potential
provinces.education: Université Kongo (Mbanza-Ngungu); relatively good school coverage

provinces.name: Kwango
provinces.economy_specialties: Subsistence agriculture (cassava, millet), livestock, cross-border trade with Angola
provinces.particularities: Heartland of the historic Yaka kingdom; Kwango River valley
provinces.education: Limited; ISP Kenge; low school coverage in rural areas

provinces.name: Kwilu
provinces.natural_resources: Oil palm, fertile agricultural land, timber
provinces.economy_specialties: Main food basket of Kinshasa (cassava, maize, palm oil); Kikwit is the commercial hub
provinces.particularities: Kikwit was the site of the 1995 Ebola outbreak; cradle of the 1964 Mulele rebellion
provinces.education: ISP Kikwit, Université de Bandundu; dense network of church schools

provinces.name: Maï-Ndombe
provinces.economy_specialties: Forestry, fishing, world-first jurisdictional REDD+ carbon program
provinces.particularities: Lake Maï-Ndombe; part of the Cuvette Centrale peatlands, one of Earth's largest carbon stores
provinces.education: Very limited; low literacy; schools concentrated around Inongo

provinces.name: Kasaï
provinces.economy_specialties: Artisanal diamond mining, agriculture, trade with Angola
provinces.particularities: Epicenter (with Kasaï-Central) of the 2016-17 Kamuina Nsapu insurgency
provinces.education: Limited; ISP Tshikapa; schooling heavily disrupted by the 2016-17 crisis

provinces.name: Kasaï-Central
provinces.economy_specialties: Agriculture, rail hub on the Lubumbashi-Ilebo line
provinces.particularities: Kananga is one of the country's largest cities; origin of the Kamuina Nsapu movement
provinces.education: Université Notre-Dame du Kasayi (UKA); strong Catholic school network

provinces.name: Kasaï-Oriental
provinces.economy_specialties: Diamond economy; historically the world's largest industrial diamond producer
provinces.particularities: Smallest province; highest population density outside Kinshasa; economic decline tied to MIBA's collapse

provinces.name: Lomami
provinces.economy_specialties: Agriculture (maize, groundnuts); Mwene-Ditu is the rail/commercial hub
provinces.particularities: Crossroads between the Kasaï and Katanga regions

provinces.name: Sankuru
provinces.economy_specialties: Agriculture and forest products; very isolated
provinces.particularities: Birthplace of Patrice Lumumba (Onalua); Sankuru Nature Reserve, key bonobo habitat

provinces.name: Maniema
provinces.economy_specialties: Mining, river transport on the Lualaba (upper Congo)
provinces.particularities: Historic Swahili-Arab trading corridor (Tippu Tip era); Kindu river-rail junction

provinces.name: Sud-Kivu
provinces.economy_specialties: Artisanal mining, highland coffee and tea, fishing
provinces.particularities: Kahuzi-Biega NP (Grauer's gorilla, UNESCO); Panzi Hospital of Dr Denis Mukwege (Nobel Peace 2018); conflict-affected (incl. M23 crisis 2024-25)
provinces.education: Université Officielle de Bukavu, Université Catholique de Bukavu

provinces.name: Nord-Kivu
provinces.natural_resources: Coltan, cassiterite, gold; very fertile volcanic soils
provinces.economy_specialties: Mining, coffee, cross-border trade with Rwanda/Uganda; tourism (pre-conflict)
provinces.particularities: Virunga NP, Africa's oldest park (mountain gorillas); Nyiragongo volcano (eruptions 2002, 2021); epicenter of the M23 conflict — Goma seized in Jan 2025
provinces.education: Université de Goma; schooling heavily disrupted by displacement

provinces.name: Ituri
provinces.natural_resources: Gold (Kilo-Moto belt), oil potential (Lake Albert), timber
provinces.economy_specialties: Gold mining, fishing (Lake Albert), livestock
provinces.particularities: Okapi Wildlife Reserve (UNESCO); recurring intercommunal violence (CODECO); Ituri rainforest

provinces.name: Haut-Uele
provinces.natural_resources: Gold (Kibali, one of Africa's largest gold mines)
provinces.economy_specialties: Industrial gold mining, agriculture (rice, coffee)
provinces.particularities: Garamba NP (northern white rhino now extinct there); historically hit by LRA incursions

provinces.name: Tshopo
provinces.economy_specialties: River trade hub at the great bend of the Congo, timber, fishing
provinces.particularities: Largest province by area; Boyoma Falls with the famous Wagenia fishermen; Lingala-Swahili linguistic frontier
provinces.education: Université de Kisangani (UNIKIS), major biodiversity research center

provinces.name: Bas-Uele
provinces.economy_specialties: Subsistence agriculture; formerly coffee and rice
provinces.particularities: Least populated province; Bili forest, home to a famous chimpanzee population

provinces.name: Nord-Ubangi
provinces.economy_specialties: Coffee, subsistence agriculture
provinces.particularities: Gbadolite hosts Mobutu's ruined palace complex ('Versailles of the jungle') and an oversized international airport

provinces.name: Mongala
provinces.economy_specialties: Congo River ports, plantation agriculture (declining)
provinces.particularities: Lisala is the birthplace of Mobutu Sese Seko

provinces.name: Sud-Ubangi
provinces.economy_specialties: Agriculture, cross-border trade (CAR, Congo-Brazzaville)
provinces.particularities: Hosts one of the largest Central African Republic refugee populations

provinces.name: Équateur
provinces.economy_specialties: River trade, forestry, fishing
provinces.particularities: Crossed by the Equator line; Cuvette Centrale peatlands (world's largest tropical peatland complex); Ebola outbreaks 2018 and 2020 in Mbandaka

provinces.name: Tshuapa
provinces.economy_specialties: Subsistence agriculture; among the most isolated provinces
provinces.particularities: Salonga NP, Africa's largest rainforest park (UNESCO), stronghold of the bonobo

provinces.name: Tanganyika
provinces.natural_resources: Tin, coal, gold; major lake fisheries
provinces.economy_specialties: Fishing on Lake Tanganyika, rail-lake transport hub at Kalemie
provinces.particularities: Lake Tanganyika (world's 2nd deepest lake); Twa-Bantu intercommunal conflict; large displaced population

provinces.name: Haut-Lomami
provinces.economy_specialties: Agriculture (maize), rail junction at Kamina
provinces.particularities: Kamina strategic military base; Upemba NP and Lake Upemba wetlands (shared with Lualaba); heart of the historic Luba empire

provinces.name: Lualaba
provinces.natural_resources: Copper and cobalt (world-class deposits: Tenke Fungurume, Mutanda, KOV, Kamoa-Kakula)
provinces.economy_specialties: Core of the copper-cobalt belt; single largest source of the world's cobalt supply
provinces.particularities: Kolwezi is one of Africa's fastest-growing mining cities; Kamoa-Kakula is the world's largest new copper mine
provinces.education: Université de Kolwezi; mining training institutes

provinces.name: Haut-Katanga
provinces.economy_specialties: Industrial mining (Gécamines legacy), trade corridor to Zambia (Kasumbalesa)
provinces.particularities: Lubumbashi, 2nd city and historical mining capital; Kundelungu NP with Lofoi Falls, one of Africa's tallest
provinces.education: Université de Lubumbashi (UNILU), one of the country's top universities
